questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to try sometghing completly new and explore a part of the world uknown to me. Plus it was cheap and i wanted to go to Asia lol

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Amazing doesn't even cover it. I came here to learn about new cultures, nature ect. and Taiwan did NOT disapoint - it is beautiful and rich in culture and such an experiance. Only downside is accomodation. 
Also some parts of the university itsself wasn't perfect.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Totally fine. I had researched courses beforehand and had help from the university with pretty quick answers. It took some effort to keep an overview of everything tho - definitly check your email often and read every detail.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Everyone was appointed an NTU student who would assist you and answer questions. Bless mine for answering my 5000 questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Made everything a lot easier especially since i didn't spend that much time preparing before leaving. Also gave a hugeee help to feel more safe entering a whole new part of the world alone.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Was super easy - NTU has recomendations for off campus housing that they trust. 
I rented my own appartment via. MyRoomAbroad because I wanted a completly non-university housing so that I could accomodate my partner from Denmark that would be staying there for a long time. But if you do not have a specific reason to stay out of the university system, I would go for something with other students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Most of the off-campus accomadation is still a dorm-style or collective living style. I know many others who also lived in a proper appartment with friends they met along they way. Many also changed housing through the semester. 
One of the other reason i wanted to be off-campus is so i could have more freedom (no cerfew or limitations of visiters and no roommate). 

But if I should say something it is to not stress too much about getting on-campus accomodation cus there are many nice social places available. Only thing is that on-campus is SO much cheaper.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Availability was pretty good but I would really suggest to not risk it with the on-campus housing.
I know multiple people that found out they did not get a dorm just a few weeks before leaving and arriving almost homeless. They of course all found stuff after not to long time but i personally would not beable to handle the stress.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Pretty stressful because I thought iIhad everything prepared and knew what I wanted, but you really only know what courses you will have 2-3 weeks into the semester.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
It was split into like 4 parts... both a blessing and a curse
They have a new and very easy to follow course website which was a big help (the one i was looking at from home was from like 2005)
1st round is applying to (only some) of the courses you want online
2nd round is applying again if you did not get the first ones you wanted AND showing up to the first class and getting a code to add the course
3rd and 4th were repeats of the above. 
Honestly is was a mess but amazing once it was over!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My NTU buddy was a big help. Also contacting teachers is most of what you have to do.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
Many were overlapping (I did not know how to find the class times before coming here) so even though I had forhåndsgodkendelse for 15 subject many of them overlapped and I only had few left. 
This lead to a pretty stressful couple of first weeks in Taiwan, as I no longer had the many backup courses I had for safety. So when i found out there was a course that I was signed up for that i didn't like/ was too hard etc. I had to find completly new ones and try again with applyig for forhåndsgodkendelse.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Please register for as many courses a possible for forhåndsgodkendelse. We're talking double minimum.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Honestly i was there for the vibes.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Even the masters course I had was mad easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
So very different in almost every way that is makes it hard to compare. 
The final grade was split into a bunch of different part like Attendance 10%, Pop Quiz 10%, Assignments 30%, Group Project 30%, Final Exam 20%. This is accutally from one of my courses - so weird to me. 
Also NO feedback on anything I did which I HATE.

This system made it so easy to be a free-spirited exchange student like me, but personally it made it so I barely learned anything.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
IPCS5063      Citizen Science: Multiple Perspectives on Participation
Geo1008       Introduction to Field Geology (Ⅱ)
MDR7910      Impact of Climate Change on Geological Carbon and Water Cycle
Phy1039        International Companions for Learning
Forest 5035   Exploring Taiwan: natural environment and resources
Geo4017       Observaing the Marine Environment
Geo4018       Field and Lab for Observing the Marine Environment

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Must have courses are: 
Introduction to Field Geology (Ⅱ) - a 4 day field trip made for NONE geologist so suuuper basic and the best trip i had in Taiwan seeing places you never could see alone. And make plenty of friends!

Exploring Taiwan: natural environment and resources - made for exchange students and one of the easiset but most interesting courses! I got to taste high quality Taiwanese tea and hold a Taiwanese snake!

International Companions for Learning (ICL) - This is one of those that you should go for if you find it interesting and if you need some credits. Every week you have a 45 min online meeting with a Taiwanese middle/ high school class in Taiwan and you tell them about you home country. In the end, you will get a field trip to go visit the school! It is fun and i loved my class, but it is not for everyone i suppose.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
THE COST OF MEDICAL EXAMINATION BEFORE DEPARTURE. WHAT DO YOU MEAN I NEEDED AN XRAY FOR 1000KR AND A HEALTH DECLARATION FOR 1000KR AND MORE. Booooo
Also I ended buying a bicyle helmet and rice cooker + new adaptors.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everthing is sooo cheap BUT if you are like me, it leads to a trap where this makes you buy way more than you should and therefore also make it more exspensive in the end of the day. But i do not regret it hihi being in a country this cheap let me live like a KING for 4 months. It was truely a blessing 10/10 reccomend.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't join any clubs and most of them were in chinese or wanted 1 year exchange students. But they did host a good amount of fun stuff like celebrating festivals, night market tours etc.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Same as above.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Keep an eye out for events on NTUmail they often come pretty late notice.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go see nature! Never have i been this close to all the nature I ever could dream of PLEASE spend as much time out there as you can. 
There are so many good day trips.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Hard tbh but friends and the university made things so much richer.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Language was acctually better than i had feared.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: No much new i loved it all. I also loved hearing about the indigenus Taiwanese.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do it! Also don't let anyone tell you the "wrong" or "right" way to be on exchange. Be as social or anti-social as you want, explore the whole island or find a few places that you love and visit often. This expernce is for you, not for anyone else.
And don't stress about "Making the most of it". You are there, that is alreadyn one big step.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can do all the medical check after you have arrived in Taiwan!!!!!!!!!!!!! I wish I knew this it would have saved SO much money and stress.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All of it. Challenges included, everything was a new experience that I would not be without.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The preparation before exchange and the course selection. And that i hated my horrible, mold-ridden, lice-ridden appartment. Glad to never enter that room again.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Do it do it do it!! Taiwan is amazing and very very interesting in every way lol. If you are up for getting out of your comfort zone this is the place.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
